sections.h2: Where do I go with a Person County property tax question?
sections.html:
Start with the Person County Tax Office at 13 Abbitt Street in Roxboro. Written appeals and abstracts go to the Tax Assessor at PO Box 1116, Roxboro, NC 27573, and the phone line printed on the county appeals page is (336) 597-1721.

The office values real and personal property for the whole county, and the commissioners set the rate. The county's reappraisal page explains that the rate is worked out each year after the board decides how much tax revenue it needs to fund services such as law enforcement, schools, solid waste, emergency services, the library, health and social services, recreation and agricultural extension. It is finalized when the commissioners adopt the budget in June.

  • Email for appeals: the county names tax@personcountync.gov as the preferred way to send an informal appeal.
  • Mail: Person County Tax Assessor, PO Box 1116, Roxboro.
  • Drop off: the Tax Office on Abbitt Street.

If you are selling a house in Roxboro or the surrounding county, the same office can tell you the assessed value on the record and whether any relief program is attached to the parcel.

sections.h2: When did Person County last reappraise property?
sections.html:
Person County's most recent general reappraisal reset all real property to market value as of January 1, 2025. Notices of value were mailed on February 1, 2025, and owners who thought the number was wrong were told to return the form before March 1, 2025.

Those dates have passed. What stays useful is the method: the county says value reflects sales of comparable property in the same local area, replacement cost of structures, potential income, location, property type, and the age, size, quality, condition, style and obsolescence of improvements. If an owner finds the market value correct, the county says no action is needed.

State law sets the outer limit. Every county must reappraise all real property at least every eighth year, and a county may choose a shorter cycle (G.S. 105-286). Ask the Person County tax office when the next reappraisal date is scheduled. The county's 2025 schedule of values stays the reference until then, and the property record card shows how a given house was priced.

sections.h2: How does the informal appeal work in Person County?
sections.html:
An informal appeal is the county's first step, and the county says most owners choose it. You file it with the Assessor's office using the informal appeal form that comes with your notice of value, and county appraisers review it without a hearing before the Board of Equalization and Review.

The appraisers may check details such as year built, square footage, number of bathrooms and other features that affect value. Send a daytime phone number and all supporting documents with the form. The county states that an appeal cannot begin until the completed form arrives.

After review, the Assessor's Office writes to tell you of any change to the value. You then decide whether a formal appeal is needed, and the county says filing informally does not cost you the right to appeal formally later.

The formal route runs through the county Board of Equalization and Review, which meets between the first Monday in April and early May to start, and which by state law hears a request made before it adjourns (G.S. 105-322). A further appeal to the Property Tax Commission is due 30 days after the board mails its decision (G.S. 105-290). Ask the office for the current year's meeting dates.

sections.h2: What relief programs does Person County offer homeowners?
sections.html:
The county page lists the three state programs, all for a primary residence only, with a filing deadline of June 1. Each of them uses the 2026 income figures below as printed by the county.

Person County homestead relief for 2026, as printed on the county relief page
ProgramMain terms
Elderly or disabled exclusionIncome $38,800 or below; 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1; reduction of $25,000 or 50% of value, whichever is greater, on the home and one acre
Veterans exclusionHonorably discharged and 100% disabled from a service injury; $45,000 off the value of the home and one acre
Circuit breaker65 or disabled; five years of ownership and occupancy; income up to $58,200; tax limited to 4% of income at $38,800 or less, 5% above that; annual application

The circuit breaker defers the excess tax as a lien. Death of the owner, transfer of the property or ceasing to use it as a permanent residence triggers rollback of the last three years of deferred tax plus interest. When several owners hold title, all must apply and qualify, though a married couple holding as tenants by the entirety does not count as multiple owners.

The county also has a land use and deferral page for farm and forest land, where deferred taxes become due for the current year plus three prior years if eligibility ends. Applications for the homestead programs are available from the Tax Office.

sections.h2: How do due dates and interest work for Person County taxes?
sections.html:
North Carolina sets one calendar for every county. Property taxes are due September 1, and bills may be paid without interest through January 5 (G.S. 105-360). Interest starts January 6 at 2%, then three-quarters of 1% for each month or part of a month after February 1.

  • Personal property is listed in January, and the state listing period runs through January 31.
  • A county can extend listing for good cause, but not past April 15 for an individual extension.
  • Mailed payments count as received on the Postal Service postmark date.

Ask the Person County Tax Office for its bill mailing date, payment methods and any prepayment discount for the year you are selling.

sections.h2: How are Person County taxes handled when a house sells?
sections.html:
The annual tax lien attaches to the parcel as of the listing date, with penalties, interest and costs added to it (G.S. 105-355). A buyer takes the property subject to unpaid tax unless it is cleared at closing.

That is why the closing attorney requests a payoff from the tax office. If the taxes for the current year are not yet billed, the parties usually agree how to split them. If you are behind, the county can foreclose the lien by court action, with sale at public auction and a redemption right before confirmation (G.S. 105-374).

  • Ask the office for the balance on each parcel, including land under farm use.
  • Check for deferred taxes under a relief or use-value program before you set a closing date.
  • Keep the final paid receipts with your closing file.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Person County property value?
faqs.a: File the informal appeal form that came with your notice of value, with your phone number and supporting records, by email to tax@personcountync.gov, by mail to PO Box 1116 in Roxboro, or at the Tax Office on Abbitt Street. If you still disagree after the written reply, you may pursue a formal appeal.

faqs.q: When did Person County last revalue?
faqs.a: The latest reappraisal used January 1, 2025 values, with notices mailed February 1, 2025. Ask the tax office for the date of the next one.

faqs.q: What is the income limit for the Person County elderly exclusion?
faqs.a: The county relief page prints $38,800 for 2026. Applicants must be 65 or totally and permanently disabled before January 1, and applications are due by June 1.

faqs.q: How much does the veterans exclusion remove?
faqs.a: The county page says $45,000 off the value of the home and one acre, for honorably discharged veterans who are 100% disabled from a service-related injury. A Veterans Disabled form accompanies the application.

faqs.q: What if I miss the property tax due date in Person County?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6 under state law, at 2% for the rest of January and three-quarters of 1% a month after that. If the tax stays unpaid, the county can enforce its lien through a foreclosure action, so contact the tax office early.
